title: Paramount Settles Antitrust Suit; $110 Billion WBD Deal Clears Final Regulatory Hurdle (September 21)
dek: Paramount resolved a multi-state antitrust lawsuit filed by 12 left-leaning states, removing the last major legal obstacle to its $110 billion acquisition of Warner Bros. Discovery. The settlement includes independent editorial boards for CNN and CBS, a $30 million-per-film penalty if Paramount misses its 30-movie-per-year commitment, and a $650 million quarterly ticking fee beginning October 1 if the deal does not close.
author: The GoCheckMySports Desk
key_fact: A trial scheduled for March 2027 is averted; the settlement clears the path for a merger that would combine CBS Sports and TNT Sports, concentrating sports rights across nearly every major U.S. professional and college league under one company.
bottom_line: The deal requires regulatory approval from any remaining entities and closes only if both companies complete their obligations by October 1 or face escalating quarterly penalties. The terms leave open how the combined operation will manage competing editorial and commercial interests across its vast sports portfolio.
body:
Paramount Global settled a multi-state antitrust lawsuit on Monday, September 21, removing the last major legal obstacle to its $110 billion acquisition of Warner Bros. Discovery, according to Front Office Sports reporting.
The deal combines CBS Sports and TNT Sports into a single entity that would hold broadcast rights across nearly every major U.S. professional and college sports league with the exception of the NBA. The settlement ends litigation that California attorney general Rob Bonta led on behalf of 12 left-leaning states, a complaint filed just over two months before the agreement was reached.
A trial in March 2027 has now been averted. Bonta stated: "This settlement is not a vote of support for this merger, or a blessing of the broader merger" and added, "Broadly speaking, we believe that further consolidation in markets that are essential to American economic life doesn't serve the economy, consumers, or competition well."
Under the settlement terms reported by Front Office Sports,  The company will, however, be subject to independent editorial boards created for both CNN and CBS. Paramount will also incur a $30 million penalty per film if it falls short of a commitment to release at least 30 movies per year, and has pledged to remain in California for several years, reversing a prior threat to relocate. Beginning October 1, Paramount faces a $650 million ticking fee for each quarter the deal does not close.
Paramount CEO David Ellison stated, "Our shared aim was an outcome that best serves consumers, workers and, most importantly, the creative community so vital to the art of visual storytelling. We're confident this agreement does exactly that."
The acquisition comes as CBS Sports reported being the league's most-watched rights holder during a banner 2025 NFL season, while TNT Sports remains in reinvestment mode following the loss of its NBA live rights. A recent WBD earnings report showed a material drop in ad sales after the NBA departure.
